articleTitle: Make2pack: a comprehensive approach to driving process and technology convergence in the CPG manufacturing and packaging sectors
publicationTitle: 2006 The Institution of Engineering and Technology Seminar on New Technology Application in Manufacturing and Supply Chain (Ref. No. 2006/11443)
abstract: The automation and packaging machinery space is undergoing fundamental change with manufacturing businesses demanding greater levels of flexibility, improved machine integration, lower capital and ownership costs and shorter delivery times from OEM suppliers. This paper offers an overview of recent technological developments in packaging machinery and will address the fundamental question about how to balance end-user integration and cost of ownership issues with OEM supply and development costs for the packaging lines of tomorrow. The ability to modularise machinery for quick changeovers and accommodate tomorrow's flexibility, traceability and shortened supply chain requirements will be key for OEMs to compete and derive industry leading ROIs for manufacturing clients. In addition to addressing the specific market drivers, this paper seeks to ascertain what keys to success lie in current standards and in particular which practical solutions can be derived from the OMAC Make2Pack initiative, the ISA/ANSI S88.05 or it's equivalent the IEC 61512.

abstract: Presentation slides describing the main challenges affecting UK CGM factories in 2006 and describes how the factories are having to respond. The talk looks at the different aspects of manufacturing (quality, safety, cost control, etc.) and details the latest requirements. Whilst describing each specific area, the author also posses a challenge to suppliers to react to these ever more stringent requirements. The author claims that the competitive edge of CGM factories will be heavily influenced by improved services from their suppliers. The talk will be of particular interest to suppliers wanting to know the right services to offer CGM factories and to manufacturers wishing to benchmark their own areas of focus.

articleTitle: Meeting assest management and supply chain challenges - using RFID in real world applications
publicationTitle: 2006 The Institution of Engineering and Technology Seminar on New Technology Application in Manufacturing and Supply Chain (Ref. No. 2006/11443)
abstract: TrenStar is a mobile asset management company who are already making innovative use of RFID in the tracking of mobile assets such as beer kegs through their cyclical use in the brewery to distribution process. Over 3.5 million beer kegs tagged with RFID are tracked at 11 locations throughout the UK. This means TrenStar is responsible for 1.2 million scans per month, which equals to 14.3 total keg cycles per year for our customers. The deployment faced a number of challenges, but TrenStar have emerged as a key player in this field with a broader systems integration arm that has exposed them to a broad range of further HF and UHF RFID applications.
